codeReview.summary: The doctest conversion portion (VAL-POLISH-007) is correctly implemented: 3 ECS doctests converted to compilable, 2 macro docs to ```text blocks, and 6 particle.rs doctests converted with proper imports and assertions. However, the GlyphRenderPool portion (VAL-POLISH-006) has a critical bug: the pool never actually reuses RenderContext+Pixmap pairs. The acquire() method uses Option::take() which removes the pair from the pool, and the caller (rasterization.rs) never returns it. On every acquire() call, self.ctx is None (from the previous take()), so needs_realloc is always true and a fresh RenderContext::new() + Pixmap::new() is allocated every time. The pool provides zero reuse benefit — it allocates exactly as often as the pre-pool code did.

issues.description: acquire() uses self.ctx.take() which removes the (RenderContext, Pixmap) pair from the pool. The caller in rasterization.rs:219 gets ownership of the pair and drops it at end-of-scope without returning it. Since self.ctx is always None after a call, every subsequent acquire() hits the needs_realloc=true branch and allocates a fresh pair. The pool never reuses anything. Fix: the caller must return the pair to the pool after use (e.g., via a release() method, or by restructuring to borrow from the pool).

sharedStateObservations.observation: The verification step 'rg RenderContext::new katla_ui/src/text/rasterization.rs — zero in hot path' is misleading as a verification command. It only checks that the call was moved to a different file (glyph_pool.rs), not that allocation was eliminated. A better verification would check glyph_pool.rs for the pattern, or better yet, add a test that calls acquire() twice and asserts only one allocation occurs.

summary: Feature pool-vello-rendercontext-and-fix-doctests FAILS review due to a blocking bug in GlyphRenderPool. VAL-POLISH-007 (doctest conversion) passes: all 11 doctests correctly converted (3 ECS runnable, 2 macro docs to text, 6 particle.rs runnable). VAL-POLISH-006 (GlyphRenderPool) fails: acquire() uses Option::take() which removes the pooled pair, and the caller never returns it, so every call allocates fresh — the pool provides zero reuse. The fix requires either a release() method called by the caller, or restructuring to borrow from the pool instead of taking ownership.
